title: Voters Oust Notorious Pro-ICE Sheriff in Maryland
author: Alex Burness
content:
Chuck Jenkins, [the notoriously anti-immigrant Maryland
sheriff](https://boltsmag.org/frederick-county-immigration-enforcement-
sheriff-chuck-jenkins/) who boasts of having helped deport 2,000 people, was
wiped out in Tuesday’s blue wave.

Voters in Frederick County, a fast-growing and increasingly liberal area north
of Washington, D.C., denied his bid for a sixth term. They opted for his
opponent, Democrat Karl Bickel, by a margin of 56 to 44 percent.

César Díaz, president of the city council in Frederick, which is the county’s
largest city, called Jenkins’s defeat “a repudiation of evil.”

“He is the face here of cruel, inhumane federal policy,” Díaz told _Bolts_
late Tuesday. “Everybody knows somebody, or knows somebody who knows somebody,
who’s been directly affected (by ICE). He's proud of being the face of that,
and people have had enough.”

Jenkins, 70, gained national fame for his staunch support of ICE, often
appearing on Fox News and visiting with Donald Trump at both the White House
and Mar-a-Lago. He joined ICE’s 287(g) program, which deputizes local
officials to act on the agency’s behalf, in 2008, long before the program
exploded in popularity among conservative sheriffs. He was an early backer of
President Donald Trump, and vowed, during Trump’s first run for office, “As
long as I am sheriff of Frederick County, we are going to work with ICE.”

Bickel, who is 76 and worked in the sheriff’s office in the 1990s, and who had
run and lost against Jenkins in each of the previous three cycles, has vowed
not to collaborate with ICE and says he plans to dispatch his deputies to
monitor ICE activity in the county. “A lot of what ICE is doing, if a deputy
did it they’d be fired or arrested,” Bickel told _Bolts_ in August. “The use
of force, the utilization of chemical agents, things like that. It’s just not
right.”

In a brief text exchange Wednesday morning, Bickel said, “Now the real work
begins.” Jenkins did not respond to a request for comment.

Ahead of the election, _Bolts_ spoke with many immigrants in the county who
said Jenkins has, since his first election in 2006, created a culture of fear
in Frederick County, which is home to a large Latino population.

Some immigrants told _Bolts_ they’ve been living in hiding lately, frequently
unable to work and sometimes unable to obtain food and other basic needs as a
result. Many have kept their children out of school and seen family members
deported.

“We’re excited. We’re really excited,” one immigrant from El Salvador said of
the election result. His stepfather was deported under Jenkins’ 287(g)
program, and _Bolts_ is not identifying him by name because he, too, is
vulnerable to deportation.

“With him out of his position, Frederick will change for the better,” the man
added. “What happened with my stepdad—it was because of policies like his.
With him out of office, I hope it will change.”

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/IMG_8361-2400x1800.jpg)Karl Bickel has challenged
Frederick County's GOP sheriff Chuck Jenkins for each of the past four
election cycles. (Photo by Alex Burness)

Jenkins’ defeat speaks both to Frederick County’s changing demographics and to
a huge amount of organizing in recent years by immigrant rights activists in
the county and throughout Maryland. This coalition successfully lobbied the
state legislature to [ban 287(g) partnerships earlier this
year](https://boltsmag.org/maryland-new-mexico-ban-local-contracts-with-ice/)
and to install other immigrant protections—changes Jenkins and 16 other
Maryland sheriffs [vigorously
opposed](https://marylandmatters.org/2026/05/27/county-sheriffs-file-lawsuit-
challenging-community-trust-act/) and sued to prevent.

Of these 17 sheriffs, most were running for reelection unopposed on Tuesday.
That lack of competition is quite common across the country, [as sheriffs
frequently face no challengers](https://marylandmatters.org/2026/05/27/county-
sheriffs-file-lawsuit-challenging-community-trust-act/), even in some places
that are otherwise quite politically competitive.

This year’s blue wave did take out at least one other sheriff famous for harsh
policing of immigrants: [Republican Terry
Johnson](https://boltsmag.org/alamance-county-sheriff-terry-johnson-shannon-
long/), of Alamance County, North Carolina, who faced a federal investigation
for his profiling of Latinos, was denied a seventh term in office, losing
narrowly to Democratic pastor Shannon Long.

Díaz, the Frederick council president, cautioned that defeating people like
Jenkins and Johnson does not alone assuage the fears of immigrants who are
still living under the threat of ICE.

“The community is under attack from more than just Chuck Jenkins,” he said.
“But that fear did go down a tick after 287(g) was banned. Now Jenkins is
gone, and the fear goes down another tick.”
